NO RUNNER IN ENTRANCE SQUARE. No extra art/books/candles/flowers/trays/decor. No brass lamp or pleated/linen shade. Real textures and accurate source daylight, no global warm tint. Return one portrait image.

generations.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Target is this current first-pass hallway mockup implementing Entrance & Hallway V1, not an earlier design iteration.
Change ONLY the runner: retain its Heriz/Serapi angular medallions, angular corners and geometric vine border, but substantially lower motif contrast over the WHOLE RUG including border. Make the wool field FADED TERRACOTTA-BROWN with camel and SOFT charcoal drawing, softly antique-washed, partially worn-away motifs close to field in value. Not mushroom/beige, not floral, not a blurry photograph. Keep material texture sharp. The present black outlines and black border are too bold; fade them to soft muted charcoal-brown so this runner harmonises with sharp black/white geometric floor tiles.
Also shorten the rug at BOTH ends so a visible band of UNCOVERED ORIGINAL TILE about30cm separates its near edge from the stair foot, and another about30cm separates its far edge from rear doorway. Keep its width ~65–70cm, central alignment and exposed tiles both sides. No entrance-square or stair rug.
Everything else must remain EXACTLY as in this target: all stairs, panelling, wall and wood colours, three Japanese prints/black frames/wide ivory mounts and positions, newel/rail, tile pattern, doors/cupboards, architecture, garden/kitchen, lighting, camera and framing. No additions or restyling. Natural source daylight, no filter. Return one taller portrait image.

limitations: Dimensions and clearances remain unverified, especially hamper/console fit and 30cm runner end margins.
Extended upper stair wall is inferred, not measured.
Generative edits approximate fine details of tilework, glass, joinery, hamper weave, reflections and framing; original photos remain the factual reference.
Prints and new furnishings are unsourced concepts, not product selections.
